channel.title: Lean Weekly
channel.description: News about Lean, the theorem prover and programming language.

item.title: Google DeepMind uses AI agents to verify Signal's messaging security in Lean
item.description:
The researchers used AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent framework for formal software specification and verification, on Signal's post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet. The agents generated 6.5 million lines of Lean code proving the libsignal implementation correct against a human-reviewed specification; the proof assumes perfect cryptography.

Sources: news.lavx.hu

item.title: Polona Durcik registers AI-generated Lean proof on triangles in positive-density sets
item.description:
The Palomar registry entry formalizes the theorem that every Lebesgue measurable planar set with positive upper Banach density contains a translated and rotated copy of every sufficiently large dilate of any fixed noncollinear triangle. The proof was developed using GPT 6 Astra Pro with human oversight; Claude Opus 5.5 Medium generated the Lean formalization.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, durcikp/lean-trianglesinplane

item.title: Alpha Squared Labs formalizes the Atiyah–Singer index theorem in Lean 4
item.description:
The project also covers the theorem's cohomological and twisted spin Dirac formulations, and Comparator, a harness checking seven independently written propositions, reported acceptance by both Lean's default kernel and the Nanoda kernel. AI assisted with Lean statements and proof development under human maintainers' responsibility; no new mathematical theorem is claimed.

Sources: alpha-squared-labs/Lean-Atiyah-Singer

item.title: Zayn Blore machine-checks the Dixmier conjecture's failure in dimension 3 and above
item.description:
The Palomar registry entry proves in Lean that, over any field of characteristic zero and in each dimension, the Dixmier conjecture implies the Jacobian conjecture, and checks an explicit counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension of 3 or more. Its four statements are copied verbatim from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, zblore/fc-dixmier-jacobian

item.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve, with Lean proofs of its security properties
item.description:
Anthropic released FlashProve, which uses a zkSNARK (a type of cryptographic proof) to prove which AI model answered a request. Anthropic used Lean to specify FlashProve's protocol and prove completeness (honest proofs are accepted), soundness (fake proofs are rejected) and zero-knowledge (proofs hide the model's weights), and shipped an executable, provably correct Lean verifier.

Sources: anthropic.com, anthropics/FlashProve

item.title: Kiro proves properties of its own agent harness in Lean
item.description:
Kiro wrote Lean models of 26 functions from its TypeScript, Rust, and Python harness (the code managing context, permissions, and state), proving 70 of 96 properties; 18 falsified ones reproduced on the real code. “Lean’s kernel checks every proof, the real code checks every finding,” says the post, which Swami Sivasubramanian shared on LinkedIn.

Sources: kiro.dev, LinkedIn post

item.title: Thanin Quartz and coauthors prove 2×2 matrix mortality undecidable, checked in Lean
item.description:
Matrix mortality asks whether some product of matrices from a finite family equals the zero matrix; only dimension two was open, with higher dimensions known undecidable since 1970. The result holds for families of 5,799 distinct 2×2 integer matrices, and a Lean 4 formalization checks the full reduction from halting, without project-specific axioms.

Sources: arXiv:2611.06562, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Jesse Comer and coauthors present Whiel for Lean-certified relational program verification
item.description:
Whiel verifies programs whose states are database instances against Hoare specifications: an LLM proposes loop invariants, and the Vampire first-order theorem prover checks their verification conditions. An independent certifier constructs Lean proofs of the original specification or its negation; the 86 benchmark tasks have certified reference answers, 69 valid and 17 invalid.

Sources: arXiv:2611.05612, JesseComer/whiel

item.title: Naoya Yamashita releases lean-ritsuryo, Japanese statutory computation with proofs in Lean
item.description:
The Lean 4 library and CLI (Apache-2.0 license) compute periods, deadlines, ages, holidays, and taxes under Japanese law, including income and inheritance tax. The library's functions come with proofs that they compute what the provisions say, and the CLI computes by calling them; the README also links a paper.

Sources: conao3/lean-ritsuryo

item.title: Leo de Moura cuts Mathlib build instruction counts, speeds up rw tactic
item.description:
Three interpreter and Meta changes cut Mathlib build instructions by 1.8% (a cache for callee lookups), 3.7% (in-place evaluation of USize, UInt64 and Array.uget/uset primitives) and 2.7% (a cache of definition unfoldings). Two others make rw faster on large goals and on goals with shared subterms.

Sources: lean4#16153, lean4#16148, lean4#16155, lean4#16130, lean4#16131

item.title: Leo de Moura fixes three quadratic performance issues in Lean
item.description:
The issues include an Expr hash collision: chains of the same application with different lengths could share hashes, so kernel cache lookups compared them structurally and checks became quadratic. The other two are quadratic elaboration of large string-literal equalities and quadratic compilation of large list literals.

Sources: lean4#16107, lean4#16046, lean4#16049

item.title: Sebastian Graf lets Lean's vcgen tactic discharge frame conditions with frameproc theorems
item.description:
The vcgen tactic now discharges the frame condition of each framed call with a theorem named by a @[frameproc], for example one for a separation logic, so the frame condition no longer becomes a verification condition. Sebastian Graf also added the @[vcgen_simp] attribute, which collects Sym.simp theorems for vcgen.

Sources: lean4#16093, lean4#15955

item.title: Researchers formalize the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem in Lean with AI agents
item.description:
The complete Lean proof follows, result by result, the 2006 proof by Maria Chudnovsky, Neil Robertson, Paul Seymour and Robin Thomas that a finite graph is perfect (every induced subgraph's chromatic number equals its clique number) exactly when it is Berge (it and its complement lack induced odd cycles of length at least five).

Sources: mahdi-jfri/StrongPerfectGraphTheorem, palomar-registry.org

item.title: Axiom Math formalizes the Stacks Project in Lean with AI agents
item.description:
The library, Stacks, covers chapters 3 to 109 of the open-source algebraic geometry reference in over 15 million lines of code; Lean's kernel checks every proof, but only the StacksCore tier is human-reviewed. Axiom Math found several Stacks Project statements that do not hold in the generality stated and formalized corrected versions alongside counterexamples.

Sources: axiommath.ai, leanprover.zulipchat.com, AxiomMath/Stacks, stacks.axiommath.ai

item.title: Fedor Popov and Leonardo Rastelli release LeanVOA, a vertex operator algebra library
item.description:
The Mathlib-based library (11,660 Lean files, 3,752,244 lines) constructs the Moonshine module, formalizes Zhu's modular invariance and Huang's tensor categories, and proves new results, declaring no axiom of its own. Under the authors' direction, AI agents (Claude Opus, Claude Fable, Codex) wrote the Lean code and first drafts of a 2,337-page companion book.

Sources: Fedor-Popov/Lean_VOA, leanprover.zulipchat.com

item.title: Mahdi JafariRaviz's repository formalizes a quasipolynomial-time graph isomorphism algorithm in Lean
item.description:
The proof writes the whole deterministic algorithm from a paper by MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi and Mahdi JafariRaviz as one program for a simple machine and proves it gives correct answers within the time bound. Ten results from the literature, each relying on the classification of finite simple groups, serve as axioms.

Sources: mahdi-jfri/GraphIsomorphismLog2

item.title: Scott Armstrong and Ahmed Bou-Rabee fully formalize Elboim-Sly paper with AI agents
item.description:
Dor Elboim and Allan Sly proved Tóth's conjecture in five or more dimensions: the interchange process (particles swapping across lattice edges whose Poisson clocks ring), run long enough, yields a permutation with infinite cycles. Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 wrote the Lean code (about 180,000 lines), which assumes nothing the paper cites.

Sources: scottnarmstrong/elboim-sly, palomar-registry.org

item.title: Xi Yin, Michael R. Douglas and Anna Mei machine-check the Osterwalder-Schrader correspondence
item.description:
Three Lean theorems, registered in the Palomar Registry, go from Euclidean Schwinger functions to relativistic Wightman distributions and back, in every positive spatial dimension. Euclidean growth is assumed and not recovered, so the two directions do not compose to a biconditional; field operators are not reconstructed, and four conventions are weaker than textbook ones.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, mrdouglasny/OSreconstruction-comparator

item.title: Nidhal Mghirbi and Seth Douglas give Lean-checked hyperbolic counterexamples to Kaplansky's conjectures
item.description:
For every prime p, a torsion-free, word-hyperbolic group based on OpenAI's constructions fails all four group-ring conjectures in characteristic p; no torsion-free hyperbolic counterexample to any of them was previously known. Nidhal Mghirbi's Lean 4 formalization proves the main theorem, including existence forms of the random-graph estimates, and builds on OpenAI's Lean development.

Sources: arXiv:2611.04599, Apsiape/kaplansky-conjectures-hyperbolic-groups

item.title: Luk Koska, Tom Koska and Ben Koska verify GPU kernels in Lean
item.description:
The authors formalize PTX, combining an interpreter covering 81 instruction forms with the axiomatic PTX memory model, and prove correct 9 hand-written PTX entry points (454 instructions), including simple implementations of FlashAttention and a 3-kernel MoE pipeline. LLM coding agents helped write the 34,034 lines of proof, which contain no sorry or custom axioms.

Sources: arXiv:2611.04447, paperswithlean.com

item.title: LARK verifies GPU kernels against PyTorch references using LLM agents and Lean
item.description:
LARK formalizes a GPU machine model and per-operation semantics in Lean 4 once per target language (PTX, CUDA, HIP), and agents prove segment-by-segment equivalence under exact arithmetic. Of 10 production kernels from LLM serving frameworks, it verifies 9 and finds a previously unknown data race in the tenth, an llm.c softmax kernel.

Sources: arXiv:2611.02028, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Baoyu Zhang and Shengmin Zhang prove Díaz–Park conjecture, formalized in Lean
item.description:
The conjecture concerns sharpness of saturated fusion systems; the proof avoids the classification of finite simple groups and answers a question from M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver's list of important open problems. The formalization, built with AI assistance from Codex, spans Lean (61,849 lines in 957 modules) and Rocq (99,857 lines).

Sources: arXiv:2611.02043, BaoyuZhang747/sharpness-Lean-Rocq, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Sreehari Sankar and coauthors present LeanGuard, Lean-verified guardrails for AI agents
item.description:
LeanGuard checks every tool call an agent proposes against a Lean 4 policy, using a decision procedure proved equivalent to a LeanLTL temporal semantics. On Tau-Bench, unguarded Qwen agents executed at least 33 policy-forbidden calls while LeanGuard executed none, and it cut direct prompt-injection success on DTap from 57.9% to 5.9%.

Sources: arXiv:2611.02332, DebarghaG/LeanGuard

item.title: Jan Onderka, Armin Biere and Henrik Böving verify a Lean SMT-LIB parser
item.description:
The paper introduces blazing-smtlib, a Rust parsing library for SMT-LIB (a standard input format for SMT solvers), and its Lean port BSmtLib, whose optimised lexer and parser provably match a formalised SMT-LIB syntax. On 9,201 benchmark files, blazing-smtlib is more than 6 times faster than previous libraries (geometric mean); BSmtLib is faster or comparable.

Sources: arXiv:2611.00185, onderjan/blazing-smtlib, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Researchers bring effect handlers to JAX, backed by Lean 4 proofs
item.description:
Oghenevwogaga Ebresafe, Daniel Zheng, Gordon Plotkin, and Ningning Xie compile effect handlers to restricted, first-order accelerator languages via a translation that statically eliminates the handlers and preserves typing and semantics, with proofs fully mechanized in Lean 4. The design is implemented as a library for JAX, a Python domain-specific language for accelerator programming.

Sources: arXiv:2611.03918

item.title: Tau Ceti uses AI to build a library of formalized mathematics
item.description:
Human-written roadmaps specify the intended mathematics, Lean's kernel checks every proof the AI contributors produce, and adversarial AI reviewers assess whether definitions and statements match what the roadmaps intend. Incubated by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative, the project aims at reusable formalizations of "all of basic mathematics" and invites contributions from everyone.

Sources: lean-lang.org, @leanprover on X

item.title: Autoresearch, Inc. releases Silmaril: Lean models of programs and verified WebAssembly tools
item.description:
Silmaril uses Lean 4 to model programs and prove properties about them, with a library of logics, models, lambda calculi and verified translations. Its demo exercises all seven Binaryen-style WebAssembly tools and checks that run() returns 42 in both the Lean WebAssembly interpreter and Node.

Sources: hiloopai/silmaril-lean

item.title: Sébastien Celles uses Lean 4 to find correctness bugs in Go
item.description:
Inspired by julia-in-lean, the go-in-lean proof-of-concept models a bounded subset of Go (including all of math/bits), states each function's documented behaviour as a theorem, proves it with Lean's kernel and bv_decide, and turns failed proofs into Go tests. Counterexamples must reproduce in Go, and the README lists Go compiler bugs reported after human review.

Sources: s-celles/go-in-lean

item.title: Volodymyr Pavlyshyn's LeanRDF certifies RDF entailment with a verified checker
item.description:
Its Lean 4 libraries define the W3C semantics of RDF, RDFS, OWL 2 RL and EL, SPARQL 1.1 and SHACL Core. Untrusted engines, Elpi (λProlog) and oxilite (a SPARQL store on SQLite), find answers that the checker turns into theorems, and the SPARQL evaluator and SHACL validator are proven to compute their semantics exactly.

Sources: Volland/rdf-lean

item.title: Darius Foo and coauthors reconstruct the Iris base logic in Lean
item.description:
Indirection Theory is simpler than Iris, thanks to ordinary dependent types, but less expressive; the authors' lightweight Lean mechanisation generalises it to Iris-style resources. Two case studies, including a program logic complete enough to verify concurrent and higher-order programs, show the base logic is expressive and faithful to Iris.

Sources: arXiv:2610.41202

item.title: Zayn Blore proves in Lean that the Poisson conjecture is false
item.description:
Following the explicit counterexample in Christopher D. Long's unrefereed 2026 preprint, the proof shows the conjecture (every substitution preserving the canonical Poisson bracket is invertible) fails for two canonical pairs and hence for every number of pairs from two up. It proves four statements from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures, with their definitions copied verbatim.

Sources: zblore/fc-poisson-2, palomar-registry.org

item.title: Harsh Gupta's Lean 4 submission ranks first in the $12 server challenge
item.description:
Harsh Gupta announced on X that the ranking is now official, with the submission serving more users than Rust, C, or handwritten assembly. The post credits the challenge's creator with explaining how Lean 4 lets developers create software more optimized than handwritten C.

Sources: @hargup13 on X

item.title: Basis Research Institute proves compiled libtommath correct in Lean, finds bugs
item.description:
The proofs show that all 100 functions of the RV64I image of libtommath v1.3.0 (76 libtommath functions and the 24 newlib/libgcc routines they call) meet specifications as total-correctness triples on the Sail RISC-V model. Bugs found in that version include mp_invmod returning −2 for -3 and 7 instead of an inverse.

Sources: BasisResearch/verified-libtommath

item.title: Junpeng Ren disproves the pure semisimplicity conjecture, with a Lean formalization
item.description:
The conjecture asserts that every right pure semisimple ring (one whose right modules are all direct sums of finitely generated modules) is of finite representation type. Junpeng Ren's triangular ring is right pure semisimple but not of finite representation type, and all sixteen labelled statements of the manuscript have compiled and audited Lean counterparts.

Sources: arXiv:2610.39883, oasisss6666/pure-semisimplicity-lean

item.title: Denis Firsov verifies worst-case constant-time order maintenance in Lean 4
item.description:
No order-maintenance algorithm (keeping a sequence under insertions and deletions and telling which of two elements comes first) had been verified in a proof assistant. This verification, about 78,000 lines, proves that a program for a step-counting machine embedded in Lean matches a reference specification within a fixed number of steps per operation.

Sources: arXiv:2610.38616, dfirsov/order_maintenance, paperswithlean.com

item.title: Lean becomes first to formalize all 100 theorems on Freek Wiedijk's list
item.description:
Freek Wiedijk's page tracking formalizations of 100 theorems, last modified October 29, 2026, shows Lean at 100, with HOL Light and Isabelle next at 95. Kim Morrison reports that the 100th theorem completed in Lean, a strong formulation of Green's theorem (TauCeti.Green.green_ac_index_one), landed in Tau Ceti, a library of AI-authored Lean mathematics.

Sources: kim-em.github.io, cs.ru.nl, taucetiproject.org, leanprover.zulipchat.com

item.title: Mathstodon user markusde posts about porting xv6 to Iris-Lean
item.description:
The post includes one attached image and thanks @ahuoguo for noticing the update.

Sources: mathstodon.xyz

item.title: Juan J. Manfredi completes Lean formalization of OpenAI's infinity-harmonic estimates
item.description:
The formalization, built on Mathlib, proves the main results of OpenAI's 4 October 2026 preprint, including that infinity-harmonic functions (viscosity solutions of the infinity-Laplace equation) on connected open sets in dimensions 3 and higher are C¹, using only Lean's three standard axioms. Claude agents wrote the Lean proofs with Trellis, an AI-assisted formalization pipeline.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, na0b/infharmonic-lean

item.title: Anthropic publishes Lean formalization of Claude's refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis
item.description:
Anthropic's eth/ project, a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization, states that a single deterministic Turing machine counts the satisfying assignments of every k-CNF with at least two clauses on at least four variables, each of which occurs, within a step bound that refutes the hypothesis. Claude's paper is in the project folder.

Sources: anthropics/formal-math

item.title: XTX Markets gives £5 million to Imperial College London for Langlands Lab
item.description:
The lab for AI-assisted mathematics, led by Kevin Buzzard, will focus on the Langlands program, which seeks connections between fields, particularly number theory and analysis. It aims to produce new results verified in Lean and begins operating in 2027, with the grant supporting five PhD students and three postdoctoral researchers over four years.

Sources: imperial.ac.uk

item.title: Leo de Moura speeds up kernel checking of lia and grind proofs
item.description:
Lean's lia (cutsat) now shares proofs across grind case splits, for up to 2.8x faster elaboration and up to 200x faster kernel checking on goals with many case splits. Kernel-friendly certificates for lia, grind's ring solver, simp +arith and grind linarith followed; the ring certificates cut kernel instructions by 51.5% across 40 benchmark files.

Sources: lean4#15905, lean4#15911, lean4#15943, lean4#15981, lean4#15983

item.title: Sebastian Graf merged vcgen +jp, which verifies code after a split once
item.description:
Without +jp, vcgen copies the code after an if or a match into every branch, so the number of copies doubles with each consecutive split. With +jp, VC generation grows linearly with the number of splits, and the shared code is verified under a hypothesis stating what each branch knows at its end.

Sources: lean4#14398

item.title: Leo de Moura makes grind failure messages short by default
item.description:
Pull request #15906 made diagnostics opt-in via +verbose, so failures showed only the remaining goal and a hint; collecting and printing diagnostics took about 38% of the time spent on easy failing lia goals. Pull request #16073 shortened the failure message further, naming the invoked tactic, such as lia, without printing the goal.

Sources: lean4#15906, lean4#16073

item.title: Mac Malone opens Lake pull request to reduce build-store contention
item.description:
The pending change (#15805) has Lake first fetch transitive artifacts from a single build-store snapshot, falling back to the real build store only when an artifact is missing. Mac Malone also opened #16083 to benchmark Lake's module setup computation, which experiments show is a significant scalability chokepoint in projects with thousands of modules.

Sources: lean4#15805, lean4#16083

item.title: Benjamin Pierce announces Agentic Proof Engineering, a Spring 2027 course at Penn
item.description:
The semester course is on building formal proofs about software systems at scale, in collaboration with AI agents, and will also be delivered as a live webinar for participants outside Penn. Some lectures and projects will be phrased in terms of Lean, though fluency with the specifics of Lean will not be needed.

Sources: cis.upenn.edu

item.title: GenProof paper on verifying Minecraft redstone circuits uses Lean's bv_decide
item.description:
Mike Murunov and Maksim Borisov's gate accepts a redstone layout only with a machine-checkable certificate of equivalence to its Verilog specification. Lean 4 re-proves the claim, unfolding it to one 4-bit equation per node and calling bv_decide, which bit-blasts, runs the CaDiCaL solver and checks its proof with a verified checker.

Sources: paper (pdf)

item.title: Troy Lee formalizes László Babai's graph isomorphism algorithm using an AI agent
item.description:
With László Pyber's analysis replacing the classification of finite simple groups, the formalization proves that a single-tape Turing machine (Mathlib's Turing.TM0) decides whether two simple graphs are isomorphic within a quasipolynomial number of transitions. The agent (Claude Code, with Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the Lean code from 18 to 29 October 2026.

Sources: palomar-registry.org, troyjlee/graph-iso-lean

item.title: Adam Gall publishes lean-sudo, a drop-in sudo replacement written in Lean 4
item.description:
Its policy, environment and authentication logic is formally verified, with 498 hand-written theorems. On Ubuntu, lean-sudo reads the existing /etc/sudoers, /etc/sudoers.d and /etc/sudo.conf, uses the system's PAM stack, and passes the same 1113-test end-to-end suite as the original sudo, a large C program written around 1980 with a decades-long history of security bugs.

Sources: adamgall/lean-sudo

item.title: holmesworcester publishes Lean Quiet, a chat app written mostly in Lean
item.description:
The iOS and Android app uses Lean for everything from TCP packets to pixels; 429 of its 586 theorems are about the code that runs. Because it is local-first, end-to-end encrypted, and peer-to-peer, many properties that would normally depend on a server operator are provable over all possible deployments, assuming user device integrity.

Sources: holmesworcester/lean-quiet

item.title: Scott Armstrong and Zohar Komargodski formalize the positive-measure KAM theorem in Lean
item.description:
The headline theorem is proved: for a nearly-integrable Hamiltonian with a small enough perturbation, most of phase space is filled by invariant tori carrying quasi-periodic motion. Agents prove the frozen statements (approved line by line, never edited); 11 of 22 are proved so far, with 73,724 of an estimated 117,000 lines of Lean.

Sources: scottnarmstrong/KAM-dev
